## Current caption

> The two solar times set against each other. A clock keeping mean solar time divides the day into equal intervals; a sundial keeping apparent solar time does not, because the Sun's apparent motion along the ecliptic is not uniform. The offset between their noons is the equation of time, and on most days of the year it is not zero.
